correctness.rationale: For the explicitly specified rooted comb and unweighted parent shift, S^n(S^n)* is diagonal with entries equal to nth-generation descendant counts. A spine vertex j has one continuing spine descendant plus one per branch in A_alpha∩[j,j+n−1], while tooth vertices have one. For beta=1/alpha>1, convexity bounds the maximum branch count by n^alpha+O(1) and j=0 attains that order; n=1 gives norm sqrt2. Increasing branch gaps imply every fixed-n diagonal except finitely many entries is <=2 and infinitely many equal 2, so all positive-power essential norms equal sqrt2. SS*>=I gives a right inverse Q of norm <=1, enabling Neumann-factor surjectivity S−lambda for |lambda|<1; infinitely many disjoint sibling differences give infinite nullity, so the Caradus Rota universality criterion applies. The spectral radius from power norms and inner eigenvalues gives closed unit-disk spectrum. Neumann resolvent sum gives O(epsilon^-1-alpha/2); normalized tooth-ray inputs on ~N^alpha branches in [N,2N) produce >=cN sqrt(N^alpha), proving a matching lower bound. Power-growth exponents distinguish alpha up to similarity. Finite check_comb.py diagnostics are supplemental only.

originality.rationale: PASS at best of knowledge: Buckley–Seco parent-shift work gives a general descendant-count formula and a universality theorem under disjoint-branch assumption (A4), which this single-spine comb fails; direct surjectivity and infinite kernel are proved here. Older directed-tree weighted shifts and Cesaro-space tree operators provide different operator models and do not deliver this exact unweighted Hilbert-space package of n^(alpha/2) growth, constant essential powers, universal open disk and exact resolvent exponent. The paper could be covered by a yet-unread general sparsely branching shift theorem, noted as risk.
residual_risks: Full Buckley–Seco text unavailable because arXiv/OA attempts failed and Oxford required manual VPN connection; the exact breadth of its later results was not checked.
A general shift-on-tree theorem under alternate Cesaro/weighted terminology might subsume part of the profile, but no same-object implication identified.
Sharp resolvent means two-sided asymptotic bounds, not an explicit leading constant or universality at the circle.
